sections.h2: Options for selling in Toms River
sections.html:
Toms River owners can list with an agent, sell privately, or take an as-is offer from a cash buyer. The right choice depends on the house, the calendar and how much repair work you want to finance before closing.

The township spans mainland neighborhoods, bayfront streets and barrier-island blocks, so a house in Silverton does not sell the same way as one in West Dover or Ortley Beach. A listing exposes the property to the most buyers and sets the price by comparison with nearby sales. A direct sale is quicker and generally leaves repairs and township paperwork on the buyer's side of the table.

The estimated population is 100,899 as of July 1, 2025, up 5.7 percent from April 2020. Of 38,047 households, 82.1 percent own their home, and the middle home value is $416,700. Median gross rent is $1,726 and median household income is $99,547. About 21.0 percent of residents are 65 or older.

Mainland addresses use ZIP codes 08753, 08754, 08755, 08756, 08757 and 08739. Ortley Beach, on the barrier strip, shares the 08751 ZIP code with Seaside Heights, so use the right one on your listing.

Dover Township became Toms River by a voter-approved name change that took effect on November 14, 2006. Older deeds, title records and tax documents may still say Dover Township, so ask your title company to confirm that the legal description matches the property.

The October 2012 storm caused the township's worst flooding on record in low-lying areas, including Silverton and the downtown area. The barrier-island neighborhoods suffered even more severe damage. A mainland or barrier house that was flooded, raised or rebuilt after that storm carries paperwork that buyers and their lenders will want to see.

  • Elevation certificate and flood insurance history, if the address is in a mapped flood zone
  • Construction permits and the final Certificate of Occupancy for any raising or rebuilding
  • Records of repairs to utilities and heating equipment

Roof age, gutters and basement or crawlspace moisture are the items a buyer's inspector checks first. If you have a private well, keep a current water test on hand.

Many Toms River sellers have run a rental, either a year-round tenant or a seasonal unit near the beach. The Division of Property Maintenance's rental packet, revised October 2024, sets the rules.

Toms River rental inspection fees and rules
Rental requirementFee or rule
Inspection fee$150 per unit
Failed re-inspection$50
Amended registration$50
Year-round rental certificateValid three years from January 1 of the year issued; new inspection on a change of occupancy or ownership
Seasonal or short-term rental on the barrier islandValid April 1 through November 30; not permitted outside that window
Scheduling noticeAt least 5 days, or 10 days from May 1 to July 15

Applications go through the township's online portal and must be complete.

The same paperwork is useful to hand a buyer who plans to keep the tenants.

  • A certificate of insurance, registered each year under state law
  • A heat certificate from a professional for fuel-burning heat sources, except for seasonal barrier-island rentals
  • Proof of ownership if the property was bought within the last 6 months or the owner does not match the tax record
  • A lead-safe certificate for any one-, two- or multi-family rental built before 1978, except seasonal rentals under six months
  • An Ocean County Health Department water analysis certificate, if the house has a well

Smoke alarm rules depend on the age of the house. Homes built before 1984 need 10-year sealed battery alarms on each level, homes from 1984 to 1990 need interconnected hard-wired alarms with battery backup, and homes from 1991 on need them in every bedroom, outside the sleeping rooms and on every level including the basement. Carbon monoxide alarms go within 10 feet of sleeping areas where a home has fuel-burning appliances or an attached garage. The property maintenance office can be reached at 732-341-1000, extension 8440.

Ask the township's construction and property maintenance offices whether a resale certificate or inspection applies to your address before you sign a contract. The township's building page covers permits and final certificates of occupancy for new homes and raised homes, and any open permit should be closed out before listing.

The clerk's forms page also lists an Application for No Knock and an Affirmative Statement to Receive Real Estate Solicitations. Ask the Municipal Clerk how those forms work if buyers you did not invite keep contacting you.

sections.h2: State forms and fees at closing
sections.html: New Jersey charges the seller a Realty Transfer Fee when the deed is recorded, based on the price in the deed, with exemptions listed by the Division of Taxation. A price over $1,000,000 adds a graduated percent fee. A seller who has moved out of state prepays estimated Gross Income Tax at closing, never less than 2% of the sale price, under the GIT/REP rules. Ask your closing attorney to run the numbers early.

1. Ask the construction office about open permits and close them.
  2. Gather flood, elevation and repair records if the house was affected in 2012.
  3. If the house was a rental, collect the certificate, insurance and lead-safe papers.
  4. Confirm the legal description with your title company in case it says Dover Township.
  5. Give everything to your attorney before the contract is signed.

A cash buyer who takes the house as it stands can skip repairs, but the paperwork still has to be in order for the deed to record.

faqs.q: Is Toms River the same place as Dover Township?
faqs.a: Yes. Dover Township became Toms River Township by a voter-approved name change that took effect November 14, 2006. Old deeds and tax records may still use the Dover name.

faqs.q: How much does a Toms River rental inspection cost?
faqs.a: The township packet lists $150 for each unit, $50 for a failed re-inspection and $50 to amend a registration. The fees are non-refundable.

faqs.q: Are seasonal rentals allowed all year in Toms River?
faqs.a: No. Barrier-island seasonal and short-term rental certificates run from April 1 through November 30, and such rentals are not permitted outside that period.

faqs.q: Do I need a lead-safe certificate to sell?
faqs.a: The packet requires it for rentals built before 1978, with an exception for seasonal rentals under six months. Ask the township and your attorney whether anything applies to an owner-occupied sale.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Toms River?
faqs.a: The middle value of an owner-occupied home is $416,700 for 2020 to 2024. Your own house may sit well above or below that depending on its location, condition and flood exposure.
